explanation: The main character in the book of Joshua and leader of the people of Israel after Moses' death. He leads the Israelites into the promised land.
The holy chest containing the stone tablets with the Ten Commandments, also known as the Ark of the Covenant. It symbolizes God's presence among the people of Israel.
The river that the Israelites must cross to enter the promised land. Miraculously, the waters stop flowing when the priests carry the ark into the river.
The spiritual leaders of Israel who perform religious ceremonies and rituals. In Joshua 3, they play a central role in carrying the ark across the Jordan River.
The area that God promised to give to the people of Israel, which Joshua and the Israelites conquer after crossing the Jordan River.
A supernatural event that cannot be explained by natural laws. In Joshua 3, a miracle occurs when the Jordan River stops flowing so that the Israelites can cross it.
